newsitem.title: FRANCE: Versolato's soul-searching lights a few sparks.
newsitem.headline: Versolato's soul-searching lights a few sparks.

text.p: - When, and if, Brazilian designer Ocimar Versolato ever reaches the end of his soul-searching, Paris may well have a virtuoso clothing designer on its hands.
Until then, the fashion community will just have to bear with off-key notes that alternate with erratic moments of brilliance.
His signature ready-to-wear collection on Wednesday night was a typical example.

From unremarkable, slinky rayon knit dresses and sandals buckling heavily up the calf, Versolato switched to the Japanese influence of a striking magenta satin wrap-around mini with kimono collar, or a liquid, wing-sleeved lavender bolero.

Then he jolted to grey wool toile suits, intricately cut but not the razor-sharp tailoring he is capable of, and a violet crepe sheath with awkwardly gaping side-seams revealing five-and-dime underwear.

There were some magical sparks, as with a draped column of bronze chiffon or a slate grey mikado bustier gown sashed with copper silk. And beautifully crafted little black cocktail dresses emanated that fragile sexuality Versolato endeavours to portray.
"He has taken major strides," said Joan Kaner of Neiman Marcus department stores. "I loved the kimono effects, the irridescent chiffons. There was a beautiful mastery of draping."

Versolato has been watched very closely since being named ready-to-wear designer at Lanvin barely a year ago. His first show for the house last March was panned by the fashion press, and his second chance comes on Saturday.
On other catwalks, nakedness is making a comeback.

After the topless torsos in shows by Christian Dior and Dice Kayek this week, German designer Karl Lagerfeld focused his line for Chloe on lingerie, giving more than a peek at models' breasts beneath sheer babydolls and bare buttocks in hiked up silk panties with matching bras.
Afro-coiffed models on neck-breaking six-inch (15 cm) heels sported splashy satin bellbottoms with halter tops and skinny jackets, lace-up suede ensembles and psychaedelic LSD prints.
Chloe officials would not confirm media reports that Lagerfeld has decided to leave the house when his contract expires in March 1997.
If he does leave, Chloe will join the long list of Paris houses, including Givenchy, Christian Dior and Guy Laroche, that have had to seek new designers.
At Nina Ricci, Miriam Schaeffer revived the riding coats, starch collars and neckties of her equestrian dandy look, this time pairing them with vinyl shorts barely covering models bottoms.
These, hopefully, were theatrical props meant only for the catwalk, for who could possibly imagine Nina Ricci's mature, demure clientele showing so much at afternoon tea?

Besides the knickers -- and variations on Schaeffer's jacket in pastel brocades with matching go-go boots and an S&M evening version with bondage platform heels -- there wasn't much there unless you think flashy sequined minis under bright terrycloth coats with swan down ruffs are wearable anywhere else than to a drag club.
The fashion season, featuring nearly 90 scheduled shows and another 40 by appointment, runs through next week when Givenchy and Christian Dior are set to announce the appointment of new designers.
